name: substrate-card the semantic ladder and its generators -- qualify, do not fix
description: MINTED 2026-08-26 by 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X on Andrew-direct at the CTO~X terminal. VERBATIM: 'I would put this as Directive 11, Substrate Analysis, and register a project beneath it called NFRA_SUBSTRATECARDING.' Runs CLAUDE.md Rule 28 (THE SUBSTRATE TEST, @ec35b78c1c) across every rung, rail and generator the C3.i identity work will stand on, producing one machine-checkable SUBSTRATE CARD per subject against org/standards/SUBSTRATE_CARD.schema.json. QUALIFY-ONLY, ZERO FIXES -- the same posture as NFRA_DEPLOYCENSUS: a card names a defect and its OWNER, it does not remediate, and a finding is never a dispatch. THE END GOAL IS NOT THE CARDS: Andrew, verbatim -- 'the end goal is to basically develop a mechanical process around the materialization and tracking of c3.i'. The four-stage identity pipeline (affinity compilation -> similarity network fusion -> identity -> succession) cannot be built on substrate whose grain, state, coverage, key space and failure modes are unknown, and six separate id-space defects were measured in one day while trying. WAVE 1 SUBJECTS (bounded, known): C0, C1, C2, C3.i-as-built, D1, D2, D3, and whatever underlies comp-similar. WAVE 2 IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED: questions 1 and 4 of every wave-1 card NAME the generators and storage locations, so the wave-2 subject list falls out of wave-1 output rather than being enumerated up front. SEPARATE STANDING DELIVERABLE: a graph-object manifest -- what graph stores exist, which are heavy/authoritative vs light/traversable projections, and each tagged to its generator -- assembled from the projection_of lineage the cards carry. Andrew's concern, verbatim: 'something that is very concerning to me is not having a clear manifest of what graph objects exist and where involved in this process'.
phase: REGISTERED 2026-08-26. Rule 28 landed @ec35b78c1c; card contract landed at org/standards/SUBSTRATE_CARD.schema.json (Draft 2020-12 valid, negative control rejects an empty card). One card already exercised ahead of the project as the reference example: nerves_resolve (design SOUND; cadence NONE, persistence NONE, substrate 19.7d stale, coverage 2,249 of ~27,000 nodes, failure mode SILENT, self-test RED). || 2026-08-26 WAVE 1 DISPATCHED by 2.0.0_SA_COO~X: decomp nfra-substratecarding/20260826T172918Z @aae317509b, 61 cells over two declared planes, 4 TOs (CCX C0/C1/C2 | CCY D1/D2/D3 | COX C3.i+comp-similar | DTX graph-object manifest). 3.0.0_SA_CVO~X seated as proof-of-spec verifier. || SCHEMA v2 AUTHORED, EFFECTIVE AT THE WAVE BOUNDARY -- NOT MID-WAVE. COO~X exercised v1 during the decomp (finding 72935) and found THREE requirements living in prose a validator cannot branch on: F-1 a null coverage denominator validates; F-2 determinism=inferential validates with NO inference_detail because 'REQUIRED when...' sat in a description string; F-3 verdict SOUND validates while a row carries basis=absent. All three are the CLAUDE.md section-4 defect this project exists to measure, committed inside the project's own contract. v1 REMAINS THE FREEZE FOR WAVE 1 (Rule 27: mid-round the spec is frozen; 4 TOs and a staged verifier harness reference it, and COO~X already carries all three as TO acceptance criteria AC3/AC4/AC5). org/standards/SUBSTRATE_CARD.v2.schema.json makes them MECHANICAL for wave 2 so nothing depends on anyone remembering. Exercised: all 3 ACCEPT on v1 and REJECT on v2, with two positive controls (a fully-measured SOUND card passes; a null denominator WITH a stated reason passes). || OWED AT THE WAVE BOUNDARY, recorded so it does not decay: the L0 manifest's lineage.projection_of and co_resident_stores are STILL array-of-string and carry the same identity-jammed-into-description defect that SUBSTRATE_CARD v2 just fixed with $defs/joinable_ref (id + note, id REJECTING ' -- ' and ' ('). NOT APPLIED MID-WAVE -- 0.4.0_DT_ClientPlatform~X is writing SC-m-3 against the L0 schema right now and 2.0.0_SA_COO~X ruled this explicitly not a mid-wave act. Source finding: COO~X 73294 @d94e825bf2 -- 51 raw entries across 8 cards resolving to 43 distinct subjects, 6 with multiple spellings; a consumer at face value enumerates 51 parts where 43 exist, and THE OVER-COUNT LOOKS LIKE THOROUGHNESS. No lane could have avoided it while following the schema; the defect was the field type. || ⛔ ARCHITECTURAL CONSEQUENCE, owed at the wave boundary and STRONGER than the joinable_ref fix it supersedes in scope: 2.0.0_SA_COO~X's tension proof (73329) shows NO DEDUP HEURISTIC ON THESE FIELDS CAN BE CORRECT -- a key strict enough to catch false splits MERGES kuzu_nessie_db with s3://opal-estate-report/kuzu_nessie_db (two distinct objects, 82.5MB local vs 51.0MB in-bucket, corroborated independently at the CTO~X seat), and a key loose enough to keep them apart leaves the splits. THE IDENTITY IS NOT IN THE STRING. Therefore joinable_ref {id,note} is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT: it separates identity from description but a clean id 'kuzu_nessie_db' still names two objects. THE L0 MANIFEST MUST BECOME THE REGISTRY -- minting part_id per part, with cards REFERENCING a registered part_id rather than a free-text name. Same L1-entity-spine problem one layer down, which is why it recurs: free-text names have been asked to do an identity registry's job. NOT BUILT, NOT AMENDED MID-WAVE. || WAVE 1 DELIVERED 2026-08-26: all four TOs ACCEPTED (CCX/CCY/COX/DTX), 8 cards, 39 manifest parts, 61 decomp cells, decomp CERTIFIED. ⛔ THE HEADLINE RESULT: 22 REAL, PERSISTED GRAPH OBJECTS THAT NO WAVE-1 CARD NAMES -- including BOTH cse_test_* tables in the PRODUCTION warehouse, a 158MB orphaned rebuild set (mine, from cancelled comp-kuzu queries ~01:0x-01:3xZ), three superseded kuzu DBs, a 25MB stitch_graph.json, four warehouse snapshot tables and five .comp-graph caches. That is the answer to Andrew's founding concern for this project. The lane SUBCLASSIFIED rather than reporting a flat 26 -- 3 unbuilt C3 stages (a card naming them would be WRONG) + 1 nerves_resolve (reference, not a wave member) + 22 real -- because 'a flat 26 OVERSTATES it and I would rather hand over the smaller honest number'. || ⛔ CORRECTION TO MY OWN COMMIT 6cb34bc2ca, which is immutable and cites a SUPERSEDED FIGURE: it says '4 of 21 rows in ACCEPTED cards'. That was the DETECTOR count. AUTHOR ADJUDICATION by all three carding lanes revised every one UPWARD: CCX 4->7 of 21, CCY 3->8 of 21, COX 5->8 of 14. ESTATE-WIDE 12 -> 23 of 56 (21% -> 41%). The detector under-counts SYSTEMATICALLY, not randomly -- three lanes, three revisions, all the same direction. The v2 fix (basis_by_field + FLOOR, 6cb34bc2ca) is unaffected; only the figure cited in its message is stale. || METHOD NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE NUMBERS: every RESIDUE-1 store fell inside a limit the manifest DECLARED BEFORE the reconcile ran -- known_unsearched had said 'a store hiding as a .yaml in that tree would be missed' and four of five were exactly that. THE DECLARED LIMIT PREDICTED ITS OWN RESIDUE. A census claiming completeness would have produced the identical five stores as a FAILURE; this one produced them as a CONFIRMED BOUNDARY. Same artifacts, opposite meaning, and the difference is one field populated honestly before the fact. || ⛔ THIRD INSTANCE OF THE DERIVED-IDENTITY CLASS, and the strongest evidence yet for the part_id registry owed at the wave boundary. 2.0.0_SA_COO~X (73857): wave-2 cell ids were assigned BY SORTED INDEX, so upholding 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~Y's duplicate-subject BLOCKING (11->9 subjects, 77->63 cells) renumbered everything after the drop -- 7 LIVE CELL IDS SILENTLY REPOINTED AT A DIFFERENT SUBJECT, 14 vanished, and W2-bg-1 still RESOLVED, it just meant something else. Their line is the one to keep: 'a lane would have carded the RIGHT id against the WRONG THING, and every alignment check would have passed' -- ids resolve, subset holds, coverage closes, and the card is about another subject. All four TOs rewritten @b918167857. THE GENERALIZATION: this is the SAME DEFECT as sysi:{domain}:{sha1(anchor_node_id)} and as the 51-vs-43 spelling collisions. ALL THREE ARE DERIVED IDENTITIES -- an id computed from something MUTABLE (a list position, an anchor resource, a free-text spelling) rather than MINTED ONCE AND TRACKED. Position is just the cheapest mutable thing to derive from. A registry that mints and tracks closes all three; no amount of care closes any of them, because in every case the derived id RESOLVES CLEANLY while meaning something else. ALSO: 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~Y found the duplicates by READING THE THING, NOT THE STRING -- edgekind_semantic has ONE definition site; the apparent second was A POINTER INSIDE A STRING. A POINTER IS NOT A SUBJECT.
